info.title: Sextant API
info.description:
Machine contract of the Sextant fleet control-plane.

AUTHENTICATION. A Bearer token (personal or service), or a browser session with X-CSRF-Token on mutations. Both resolve through the same wrapper; no endpoint authenticates its own way.

ERRORS. Every failure answers application/json with the Error schema - including the refusals raised before a handler runs and a path matching no route. A 500 always carries the literal string "internal error"; the detail is in the server log, deliberately, so an error response can never leak internals.

EMPTY LISTS. A list endpoint answers [] and never null, whether or not the fleet is empty.

VERSIONING, from the 1.0 freeze:

* ADDITIVE ONLY within /api/v1. New endpoints, new optional request fields and new response fields may appear at any time. A client MUST ignore response fields it does not know - that is the whole basis of the promise.
* NEVER within /api/v1: removing or renaming an endpoint, a field or an enum value; narrowing a type; making an optional request field required; or changing the status code an operation answers for the same condition.
* If something genuinely must break, it happens under /api/v2 and the two run side by side. /api/v1 then enters a DEPRECATION WINDOW of at least twelve months from the day v2 ships, announced in the release notes and carried on every deprecated operation as `deprecated: true` in this document.
* A security fix may break the rules above. That is the one exception, it is announced as such, and the reason is published.

This spec is verified against the running server: CI fails if a route exists without a spec entry, if a spec entry has no route, if an operation does not document its errors, or if a documented response shape is not what the server writes.

group.description: The directory group the binding grants to.

role.description: The role the group gets at the scope.

scope.description: Where the role holds: "org", or a group's scope such as "group:pilot".

group.description: The identity provider group the binding is for.

AppList.description: One app list at one scope, replaced as a whole.

names.description: The complete list after this call; an empty list clears it.

Assignment.description: A policy bound to a scope, optionally narrowed by a filter.

filter.description: A filter's id; the policy then applies only to the devices it selects. Empty selects every device.

priority.description: Breaks a tie between assignments that set the same key at the same scope: higher wins.

filter.description: The filter the assignment was narrowed by, if any.

Assurance.description: The audit controls, replaced as a whole. A field left out is off.

requireFourEyes.description: A change cannot be merged by the person who made it.

requireChangeRequest.description: Settings change only through a change request, never directly.

requireTestWave.description: A rollout needs a first wave that waits for approval; an org owner may skip it for one rollout.

manualRolloutOnly.description: Merging a change starts no rollout; somebody starts every run by hand.

AuditEntry.description: One entry of the configuration audit trail. It is git history, so it is append-only and complete.

subject.description: Commit subject: what changed, in the words the console wrote.

author.description: Who made the commit, by name.

email.description: Their e-mail address, as the commit records it.

ChangeEdit.description: One setting edit on a change request's branch.

value.description: The value, typed as the catalog entry for the key says: a boolean, a number, a string or a list. Ignored with clear.

enforce.description: Lock the value, so a narrower scope cannot weaken it. Left out, the lock stays as it is.

clear.description: Remove the key at this scope instead of setting it.

ChangeRequest.description: A change request: settings edited on a branch of their own, merged into the fleet after the gate has built the devices it touches.

author.description: Who opened it, by display name.

authorSubject.description: Who opened it, by the identity provider's subject; four-eyes compares this one.

branch.description: The branch of the fleet repository it lives on.

error.description: Why the gate or the build refused it, when it did.

hosts.description: The devices its edits can reach, which the gate builds.

wholeFleet.description: An edit reached the whole fleet, so the gate builds every device.

Condition.description: A requirement on what a device reports, not on its configuration: it is checked, never written.

metric.description: What is measured, as the device reports it, for example disk.free_percent or memory.total_mb.

op.description: How the measurement compares to value.

detail.description: What a failure means, in words for whoever reads the finding.

Device.description: A device as the fleet document holds it. This is the CONFIGURATION view; what a device reports about itself is /api/v1/status.

tag.description: Stable identifier. A lowercase slug; also the machine hostname.

groups.description: Group memberships, most general first. Always an array, never null.

class.description: One of laptop, desktop, server, station. May be absent on a device a station discovered but nobody has classified.

hardware.description: Hardware profile name from the overlay.

assignedUser.description: The person this device belongs to. Personal data - see docs/compliance/processing-register.md.

DeviceDetail.description: One device: its record, the settings that apply to it and where each comes from, and its apps.

resolved.description: Every setting that applies, sorted by key.

apps.description: The apps it gets, after every scope has added its own.

DeviceFacts.description: What a device last reported about its hardware.

facts.description: The report, as the agent sent it.

DeviceIntent.description: An action for a device to carry out at its next check-in.

force.description: Wipe a device that is not locked first.

DevicePatch.description: The device fields to change. A field left out stays as it is.

hardware.description: The hardware profile the device's configuration is built for.

class.description: The device class, such as laptop.

groups.description: The groups the device is in, as a complete list.

labels.description: Free key-value labels, as a complete set.

DeviceRecord.description: A device as the fleet repository holds it.

state.description: Where it is in its life. Empty is active.

intent.description: An action waiting for its next check-in. Empty is none.

pin.description: A rollout wave's group this device follows before the rest of its group does.

groups.description: The groups it is in. Order counts: where two unrelated groups set the same key, the earlier one wins.

class.description: The device class, such as laptop.

hardware.description: The hardware profile its configuration is built for.

settings.description: Settings set on this device itself.

enforced.description: Keys among settings that cannot be changed for it elsewhere.

packages.description: Nix packages for this device itself.

flatpaks.description: Flatpak apps for this device itself.

overlays.description: Overlay modules for this device itself.

accepted.description: Accepted risks: a control's key to why it does not hold here.

DeviceStatus.description: What a device last reported about itself.

phase.description: Where it is in its installation.

error.description: What went wrong, when the device said something did.

sb.description: Secure Boot, as the device sees it. Empty when it did not say.

tpm2.description: The TPM2, as the device sees it. Empty when it did not say.

ack.description: The last action the device confirmed carrying out.

integrations.description: Each integration turned on for it, by name, as it last saw it.

online.description: It checked in recently enough to count as there.

DeviceWithCredential.description: A device that may check in again, with the credential to do it.

credential.description: The secret the device checks in with. Shown once; store it before leaving this answer.

notice.description: A reminder that the credential is not shown again.

credentialError.description: Present when no credential could be made: make one with POST /api/v1/devices/{tag}/credential before the device checks in.

DirectoryGroup.description: A group in the identity provider's directory.

error.description: Human-readable reason. Safe to show an operator: it never carries internals - a 500 is always the literal string "internal error", with the detail in the server log.

Evidence.description: What an auditor asks for over a period: the controls in force, and every commit, change request and rollout in it.

from.description: The start of the period, included.

commits.description: Every commit to the fleet repository in the period, newest first.

changes.description: Every change request touched in the period.

rollouts.description: Every promotion of a rollout wave in the period.

EvidenceControls.description: The audit controls in force when the evidence was made.

requireFourEyes.description: A change cannot be merged by the person who made it.

requireChangeRequest.description: Settings change only through a change request.

requireTestWave.description: A rollout needs a first wave that waits for approval.

subject.description: The commit that moved the wave.

Filter.description: A test on device attributes that selects devices.

name.description: A label for people; the id in the path is what refers to it.

match.description: Whether every rule must hold or one is enough. Left out, every rule.

FilterRule.description: One test on one device attribute.

attr.description: The attribute: tag, class, hardware, assignedUser, group (membership, including parent groups) or "label:<key>".

value.description: The value to compare with; for every op but in.

values.description: The values to compare with; for in.

Fleet.description: The fleet document as the fleet repository holds it in fleet.json, with only what the caller may see.

GroupPatch.description: The group fields to change; at least one. A field left out stays as it is.

parent.description: The new parent group; empty makes it a top-level group.

idpGroup.description: The identity provider group whose members belong to it.

HardwareSpec.description: The hardware an installation station found when it enrolled the device.

Health.description: systemd's last verdict on the machine.

state.description: systemd's own word, such as "running" or "degraded".

hostKey.description: The device's SSH host public key, as recorded at enrolment.

hostKeyId.description: The id of the device's SSH host key.

IntegrationState.description: One integration as the device last saw it.

state.description: "up" or "down"; empty when nobody measured, which is not the same as down.

detail.description: What the device saw, such as the address it reached.

IntentArmed.description: An action armed for a device.

IssuedCredential.description: A device credential, shown this once.

credential.description: The secret the device checks in with. The console keeps only its hash.

notice.description: A reminder that this is the only time it is shown.

Me.description: Who the caller is and what they may do. The roles map is resolved per request, never stored.

name.description: Display name from the identity provider.

email.description: E-mail address from the identity provider.

groups.description: Directory groups. Always an array, never null.

service.description: True for a service account rather than a person.

roles.description: Resolved role per scope, e.g. {"org":"editor","group:pilot":"owner"}. Only scopes where the caller holds at least viewer appear.

ceiling.description: Present only for a scoped token: the highest role it may reach regardless of the underlying grant.

id.description: The id to give it. A lowercase slug.

tag.description: Its name in the fleet. A lowercase slug.

hardware.description: The hardware profile its configuration is built for.

class.description: The device class, such as laptop.

parent.description: The group it sits in; left out, it is a top-level group.

idpGroup.description: The identity provider group whose members belong to it.

NewSecretRef.description: A secret reference to register: the name of a secret the devices get from elsewhere, never the secret.

id.description: Its id, by which it is listed and revoked. A service account becomes the principal svc:<id>.

kind.description: A personal token acts as you; a service account is a principal of its own, made by an org owner. Left out, personal.

ceiling.description: The highest role the token may use, whatever its holder has.

groups.description: For a service account: the groups it is in.

ttlDays.description: How many days it is valid. Left out, the console's default.

NewTokenAnswer.description: A token, with its secret shown this once.

secret.description: The bearer secret. Shown once; the console keeps only its hash.

notice.description: A reminder that the secret is not shown again.

Policy.description: A named set of settings and conditions, applied where it is assigned.

name.description: A label for people; the id in the path is what refers to it.

settings.description: Setting keys from the catalog, with their values.

enforced.description: The keys among settings that a narrower scope cannot weaken.

profile.description: The overlay profile the policy was made from, as name@hash. Empty for a policy made by hand.

controls.description: The compliance controls it implements, such as "BIO 12.3.1". Free text.

conditions.description: Requirements on what a device reports.

Preferences.description: Your own preferences. Empty means the organisation's default.

timezone.description: An IANA time zone, such as "Europe/Amsterdam".

ResolvedSetting.description: One setting as it applies to a device, and where it comes from.

enforced.description: A narrower scope cannot change it.

RingProgress.description: How far one wave of the active run is. The field names start with a capital, unlike the rest of the API.

Total.description: Devices in the wave so far.

OnTarget.description: Of those that are there, how many run the target.

Healthy.description: Of those on target, how many are healthy.

Broken.description: Of those on target, how many report an error or are stuck.

Absent.description: Devices not seen for a while; they do not count against the wave.

Released.description: How many of the group have been given the target so far.

GroupTotal.description: How many devices the group has.

RolloutPlan.description: The waves a change rolls out in.

autoFlow.description: Start a rollout by itself when a change reaches the fleet repository. Left out, on.

group.description: The device group the wave covers; set this or groups.

groups.description: The device groups the wave covers, when it is more than one.

name.description: A label, such as Canary or Test.

soakMinutes.description: How long the wave runs before the next may start.

minHealthyPercent.description: How many of its devices, in percent, must be healthy to go on.

requireApproval.description: Wait for somebody to approve before the next wave.

minDevices.description: How many devices must report before the percentage counts. 0 is half the wave.

maxDevices.description: At most this many devices get the change at once. 0 is the whole group.

target.description: A commit of the fleet repository.
The revision every wave moves to.

rings.description: The run's own waves, fixed when it started.

changeId.description: The change request the run delivers, when it delivers one.

ring.description: The wave it is on, counted from 0.

promotedAt.description: Per wave, by number: when it was given the target.

convergedAt.description: Per wave: when all its devices first ran the target.

approvedAt.description: Per wave: when somebody approved it.

buildRequestedAt.description: Per wave: when its build was asked for.

waiting.description: What it waits for, in words; empty once it has ended.

waitingSince.description: Since when it has waited for that.

RolloutTick.description: What one step of the rollout engine did.

state.description: The run's state after the step, as GET /api/v1/rollout answers it; null when there has never been a run.

action.description: What the step decided; absent when no run is active.

rings.description: Progress per wave of the run.

name.description: The reference a setting uses. Never a value.

value.description: The value, typed as the catalog entry for the key says: a boolean, a number, a string or a list.

enforce.description: Lock the value, so a narrower scope cannot weaken it. Left out, the lock stays as it is.

scope.description: The scope that sets it: "org", "group:<name>" or "device:<tag>".

policy.description: The policy that sets it there, when a policy does.

Status.description: The answer to a write that has nothing to return but its own success.

Token.description: An API token, without its secret.

ceiling.description: The highest role it may use. Empty is no limit beyond its holder's.

Usage.description: What the device last measured of its own load.

ChangeID.name: id
ChangeID.description: The change request's id, given when it was opened with POST /api/v1/changes. A lowercase slug.

DeviceTag.name: tag
DeviceTag.description: The device's tag: the name it has in the fleet, as GET /api/v1/devices lists it. A lowercase slug.

FilterID.name: id
FilterID.description: The filter's id. A PUT with a new id creates the filter. A lowercase slug.

GroupName.name: name
GroupName.description: The group's name, as GET /api/v1/groups lists it. A lowercase slug.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: How many items to return. Absent means all of them, which is the default and what a client written before paging existed will see. At most 1000 per request.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: How many items to skip. An offset past the end is an empty array, not an error: a list that shrank between calls is ordinary.

PolicyID.name: id
PolicyID.description: The policy's id. A PUT with a new id creates the policy. A lowercase slug.

SecretRefName.name: name
SecretRefName.description: The secret reference's name, as GET /api/v1/secret-refs lists it. A lowercase slug.

TokenID.name: id
TokenID.description: The token's id, as POST /api/v1/tokens returns it and GET /api/v1/tokens lists it. Not the secret.

XTotalCount.description: The size of the UNPAGED list, scoped to what the caller may see. Set on every list response, paged or not, so a client can learn the size without walking it.

404.description: No such endpoint, or the named resource does not exist.

409.description: The write conflicts with the current state: a lost write race, or a change-request-required policy refusing a direct write.

422.description: The resulting configuration was refused by the nix evaluation gate. The message carries the evaluator's reason.

500.description: Unexpected server error. The body is always {"error":"internal error"}; the detail is in the server log, deliberately.

503.description: A dependency the endpoint needs is not available (database, gate-runner, directory). Retry.
